summary: A granite tower and keeper's house on Lighthouse Island, lit in 1868 to mark the Huron Islands in Lake Superior; automated in 1972 and now in a wildlife refuge.

access.note: Lighthouse Island is open to the public; reached only by boat. Other refuge islands closed.

notes_for_editor: No NRHP nomination text is digitised (placeholder), so the chronology rests on Lighthousefriends (copyright; facts restated), Light-House Board reports and newspapers. 1909 wreck: Witte's account (via L'Anse Sentinel quoting Marquette Mining Journal) puts it at 11:45 Friday morning 30 April; a Washington Herald wire said after midnight and nine seamen; most papers said seven. Injuries differ between the Mining Journal and Lighthousefriends. The Bulletin passages (1916 launch Petrel; 1918 Vulcan) are dated by volume year only; day-month from the text, year inferred from the volume. Report volume for the 1890 lightning is the 1891-92 bound volume; fiscal year not determined. Fog-signal hours (1895, 1899) are from report volumes labelled by corpus year. Roster parsed from the USLHS list; 'at least' spans marked approx; Isaac Berg's 1900-1899 printed as in archive. Witte's earlier stations are from Lighthousefriends only. Lens current location unknown. Public access to Lighthouse Island is per FWS; tower interior access not stated. Fact-check 2026-10-27: Bulletin 1916 Petrel item sits in a section running May to Sept 1916 events (issue of autumn 1916); the 1918 Vulcan item (1 Nov) is at the end of the 1918 volume, year inferred. Oil house is in the 1896-97 report volume (LF dates it 1896).
